email.html:
I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys.

Matins · Tuesday, 17 November 2026

St. Gertrude, Virgin

S. Gertrudis Virginis O. N. · Duplex

Read in Latin and English

Lesson I

From the Song of Songs

Song 2:1-5

I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys. As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters. As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow, whom I desired: and his fruit was sweet to my palate. He brought me into the cellar of wine, he set in order charity in me. Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples: because I languish with love.

℟. The Lord loved Gertrude in perpetual charity, therefore he drew her to him from infancy, and led her into solitude . * and spoke to her in her heart.

℣. He espoused her to himself forever in faith and mercy.

℟. And spoke to her in her heart.

Lesson II

Song 8:6-7

Put me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thy arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy as hard as hell, the lamps thereof are fire and flames. Many waters cannot quench charity, neither can the floods drown it: if a man should give all the substance of his house for love, he shall despise it as nothing.

℟. Gertrude, speaking to her spouse, said: * But it is good for me to cling to you alone, my Beloved.

℣. Then the Lord leaning towards her, looked with desire, saying, And for you to cling to me, is always sweet, my beloved.

℟. But it is good for me to ling to you alone, my beloved.

Lesson III

Born at Eisleben in Saxony, Gertrude offered her virginity and herself to Jesus Christ in the Benedictine monastery of Rossdorf, when she was five. She had St. Mechtilde for her teacher, and under this guidance attained the highest gifts of contemplation. She burned with such love for the most holy Sacrament of the Eucharist and the Passion of the Lord that when she thought of them she shed tears in profusion. She wrote many things to foster devotion, and was known for the gift of divine revelation and of prophecy. Finally, consumed more by her burning love of God than by sickness, she departed this life, famous for miracles both before and after her death.

℟. The Most High placed Gertrude in his tabernacle, * God is in the midst thereof, she shall not be moved.

℣. God will help her early in the morning.

℟. God is in the midst thereof, she shall not be moved.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. God is in the midst thereof, she shall not be moved.

Read in Latin and English

Monastic Breviary, 1963. Texts from Divinum Officium (divinumofficium.com).
